items.text: Block embeds are back to one bullet, as in 0.8 (#417, #748). In 0.9.0-beta.1 a block embed showed two bullets, one for the block holding `{{embed ((…))}}` and one for the embedded block. Now the embedded block's bullet sits where the embed does, and dragging it, **Tab**/**Shift+Tab**, **Move block up/down**, selecting it and its menu act on the block holding the embed on that page; its text and children are still the source's. Moving it up or down therefore no longer moves the source block on its own page or shows the "moved in" notice (GH #641); page embeds, Linked References and query results keep that behaviour. Folding the embedded block is still remembered per page; folding a block further inside the embed now folds that source block on its own page and in every embed of it, as in Logseq. A block with its own text besides the embed keeps its own bullet.

regressionEvidence.reason: Catalog coverage: UI-BLOCK-EMBED-ROOT-BULLET-001, UI-GH726-EMBED-BULLET-OWNERSHIP. Gated on develop and release/0.9 (Linux native journeys).

items.text: A block inside a grid cell now looks and works as it does on a page (#782). Task markers with their checkbox, priorities, SCHEDULED and DEADLINE chips and properties show in the cell and in every block nested under it, however deep; ticking a checkbox in a cell saves the new marker. Nested blocks have the page's bullet and indent one fixed step per level instead of a step that grew with each level, so deep outlines no longer run off the cell. A sub-grid inside a cell is unchanged.
